questions.title: Who will win Okinawa's 2026 gubernatorial election?
questions.background: Okinawa is Japan's southernmost prefecture, where the presence of US military bases is a major political issue.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official results announced by Okinawa's election authorities, either directly or as reported by reliable news organizations. Resolution : The question resolves when the winner of Okinawa's 2026 gubernatorial election is officially announced. Accepted Answer Format : The winning candidate's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major final-weekend polling sweep published Sept 6 (one week before Sept 13 voting) shifts the race decisively toward five-party-backed challenger Genta Koja (0.53 -> 0.63) over two-term All-Okinawa incumbent Denny Tamaki (0.46 -> 0.365; 0.005 across four minor candidates): (1) Yomiuri Shimbun (Sep 3-6, phone+net, n=1,410) reports Koja clearly leading ('先行') with Tamaki trailing—noting 20% of 2022 Tamaki voters switched to Koja, 80% of 2022 Shimoji voters back Koja, and economy/prices (75%) dwarfs bases (45%); (2) Asahi Shimbun / Okinawa Times / QAB (Sep 5-6, phone+net) similarly reports Koja slightly ahead ('やや先行') with Tamaki chasing vigorously (40% undecided)—a striking signal given Okinawa Times/Asahi's historically All-Okinawa-favorable coverage; (3) Kyodo / Ryukyu Shimpo / OTV (Sep 5-6, pure RDD phone, 603 landline + 404 mobile) shows a dead heat ('横一線', <10% undecided), yet its internals also favor Koja: economy/tourism/jobs is the #1 issue (46%, breaking 70% Koja) vs bases (26%, breaking 80% Tamaki), and Henoko relocation support edges opposition 48%-46%. We cap Koja at 0.63 (leaving Tamaki 0.365) because pure phone polls remain tied, Tamaki leads ~60% of independents and 70+ voters (who turn out at higher rates), and 20-40% remain undecided in Yomiuri/Asahi.
